drafts.draft: A Pharisee and teacher of the law, honored by all the people, who sat in the Sanhedrin; Paul says he was educated at his feet.
verses: Acts 5:34 But a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law who was honored by all the people, stood up in the Sanhedrin and ordered that the men be put outside for a short time.

Acts 22:3 “I am a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but raised in this city. I was educated at the feet of Gamaliel in strict conformity to the law of our fathers. I was just as zealous for God as any of you are today. (Paul speaking, from Acts 21:40)

drafts.draft: Son of David, born in Jerusalem; the parallel lists in 2 Samuel 5:14 and 1 Chronicles 14:4 have Shammua in his place.

lutheran.why: Nothing doctrinal is at stake, but 'sat in the Sanhedrin' claims a membership Acts 5:34 does not state (it says he 'stood up in the Sanhedrin'), and 'he' and 'his' in one sentence point at two different men.
lutheran.wording: A Pharisee and teacher of the law, honored by all the people, who stood up in the Sanhedrin; Paul says that he himself was educated at the feet of Gamaliel.

reformed.why: The verse, not the tradition, is the check here: Acts 5:34 shows him standing up in the Sanhedrin, not seated as a member, and 'he'/'his' in the second clause is ambiguous between Paul and Gamaliel.
reformed.wording: A Pharisee and teacher of the law, honored by all the people, who stood up in the Sanhedrin; Paul says that he himself was educated at the feet of Gamaliel.

wesleyan.why: 'Sat in the Sanhedrin' states a membership Acts 5:34 does not give (it says he 'stood up in the Sanhedrin'), and 'he'/'his' names Paul and Gamaliel in the same sentence.
wesleyan.wording: A Pharisee and teacher of the law, honored by all the people, who stood up in the Sanhedrin; Paul says that he himself was educated at the feet of Gamaliel.

baptist.why: Acts 5:34 says Gamaliel 'stood up in the Sanhedrin'; 'sat in' asserts membership the verse does not state, and 'he'/'his' is ambiguous between Paul and Gamaliel.
baptist.wording: A Pharisee and teacher of the law, honored by all the people, who stood up in the Sanhedrin; Paul says that he himself was educated at the feet of Gamaliel.

pentecostal.why: 'Sat in the Sanhedrin' goes beyond Acts 5:34, which says he 'stood up in the Sanhedrin', and 'he'/'his' in the second clause reads as Gamaliel to a newcomer when Paul is meant.
pentecostal.wording: A Pharisee and teacher of the law, honored by all the people, who stood up in the Sanhedrin; Paul says that he himself was educated at the feet of Gamaliel.

catholic.why: The Church's tradition does not supply the membership claim in this sentence; the verse shows him standing up in the council, and 'he'/'his' is ambiguous between Paul and Gamaliel.
catholic.wording: A Pharisee and teacher of the law, honored by all the people, who stood up in the Sanhedrin; Paul says that he himself was educated at the feet of Gamaliel.

orthodox.why: Acts 5:34 says he 'stood up in the Sanhedrin', not that he sat as a member; the sentence should keep to that, and 'he'/'his' must be fixed so the second clause cannot be read as Gamaliel being taught at his own feet.
orthodox.wording: A Pharisee and teacher of the law, honored by all the people, who stood up in the Sanhedrin; Paul says that he himself was educated at the feet of Gamaliel.

rabbi.why: Acts 5:34 places him standing up in the Sanhedrin and does not state that he sat as a member; the sentence should say only what the verse says, and 'he'/'his' should name Paul and Gamaliel without ambiguity.
rabbi.wording: A Pharisee and teacher of the law, honored by all the people, who stood up in the Sanhedrin; Paul says that he himself was educated at the feet of Gamaliel.

young_african_american_believer.why: Plain-English check: 'he' and 'his' in one sentence point at two men, and 'sat in' adds a membership the verse does not state (it says he 'stood up in the Sanhedrin').
young_african_american_believer.wording: A Pharisee and teacher of the law, honored by all the people, who stood up in the Sanhedrin; Paul says that he himself was educated at the feet of Gamaliel.

lutheran.why: Nothing doctrinal here, but 'have Shammua in his place' asserts that Shammua and Shimea are one son; the verses give different names in the same position and do not say they are the same person.
lutheran.wording: Son of David, born in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 3:4-5); the matching lists in 2 Samuel 5:14 and 1 Chronicles 14:4 give the name Shammua in the same place where 1 Chronicles 3:5 gives Shimea.

reformed.why: Harmonising is a reading the verses leave open: they show two names in one slot and say nothing about identity, so the sentence should report the difference and not settle it.
reformed.wording: Son of David, born in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 3:4-5); the matching lists in 2 Samuel 5:14 and 1 Chronicles 14:4 give the name Shammua in the same place where 1 Chronicles 3:5 gives Shimea.

wesleyan.why: The sentence says the lists 'have Shammua in his place', which treats the two names as one son; the verses show different names in the same position and do not state identity. 'Son of David' also rests on 1 Chronicles 3:1 and 3:4, which are not among the cited verses.
wesleyan.wording: Son of David, born in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 3:4-5); the matching lists in 2 Samuel 5:14 and 1 Chronicles 14:4 give the name Shammua in the same place where 1 Chronicles 3:5 gives Shimea.

baptist.why: 'Have Shammua in his place' asserts the two names are one son, which the verses do not say; they show different names in the same position. 'Son of David' needs 1 Chronicles 3:4 cited, since 3:5 says only 'him'.
baptist.wording: Son of David, born in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 3:4-5); the matching lists in 2 Samuel 5:14 and 1 Chronicles 14:4 give the name Shammua in the same place where 1 Chronicles 3:5 gives Shimea.

pentecostal.why: The sentence treats Shammua and Shimea as one son, which the verses do not state; they give different names in the same place. 'Son of David' rests on 1 Chronicles 3:4, which is not cited.
pentecostal.wording: Son of David, born in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 3:4-5); the matching lists in 2 Samuel 5:14 and 1 Chronicles 14:4 give the name Shammua in the same place where 1 Chronicles 3:5 gives Shimea.

catholic.why: The Church's tradition does not decide this name question, and the sentence asserts an identification the text leaves open; the verses show different names in the same slot. 'Son of David' needs 1 Chronicles 3:4 cited.
catholic.wording: Son of David, born in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 3:4-5); the matching lists in 2 Samuel 5:14 and 1 Chronicles 14:4 give the name Shammua in the same place where 1 Chronicles 3:5 gives Shimea.

orthodox.why: The sentence turns a difference of names into an identity ('have Shammua in his place') that the verses do not state; the reader should see the two names side by side and not be told they are one son.
orthodox.wording: Son of David, born in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 3:4-5); the matching lists in 2 Samuel 5:14 and 1 Chronicles 14:4 give the name Shammua in the same place where 1 Chronicles 3:5 gives Shimea.

rabbi.why: The verses give two different names for the son in the same position across books; the sentence settles that they are one person, which the text itself leaves open. 'Son of David' rests on 1 Chronicles 3:4, which is not among the cited verses.
rabbi.wording: Son of David, born in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 3:4-5); the matching lists in 2 Samuel 5:14 and 1 Chronicles 14:4 give the name Shammua in the same place where 1 Chronicles 3:5 gives Shimea.

young_african_american_believer.why: Plain-English check: 'parallel lists' and 'in his place' are unclear to a newcomer, and the sentence reads as settled that Shammua and Shimea are one son, which the verses do not say.
young_african_american_believer.wording: Son of David, born in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 3:4-5); the matching lists in 2 Samuel 5:14 and 1 Chronicles 14:4 give the name Shammua in the same place where 1 Chronicles 3:5 gives Shimea.

biblical_theological.why: Plain, text-bound; 'Paul says' keeps the Acts 22 claim in Paul's voice.
